title: Correct ESC-25: the split route was taken after all
body:
One row appended to `docs/escapes.md`. No code. It carries the id **ESC-25**, the same as the row above it.

**Why a second row rather than an edit.** ESC-25 landed on #177 saying "This escape was filed instead of taking that route" — the route being `test-the-tests`'s src-only/tests-only skip. About an hour later the owner, shown the choice between merging #176 red on a required check and splitting it, **chose the split**. So the sentence is now false. This ledger is append-only and enforced, and an entry edited in place is a rewrite however little the text changes — the failure ESC-18 and ESC-19 already record. The file's own instruction is to append a correction row with the same id, which is what ESC-21 did.

**What the correction adds.** Nothing about the gate analysis changes. What changes is one fact worth having written down: the hatch is no longer merely available, this repository has now used it, and the next reader must not read the earlier row's last sentence as evidence that it has not.

And it names a gap the first row missed. **Nothing anywhere records that two green pull requests are halves of one change.** No marker, no trailer, no shared id. That a required check was skipped twice for one logical change survives only here, by hand, because someone chose to write it down.

That gap suggests a third candidate, cheaper than the two already listed and useful on its own: when a change is split to satisfy a gate, both halves carry the same declared id in their commit trailers, so the split is VISIBLE to anything reading the history. `blind-tests.sh` already proves that shape works.

Ran locally against this diff: `plan-resolve.sh` (exempt prefix `docs/`, cap 50), `escapes-append-only.sh`, `escape-refs.sh`.
